newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Farmers burn tobacco in Brussels protest.
newsitem.headline: Farmers burn tobacco in Brussels protest.

text.p: Plumes of aromatic smoke hung about the European Commission's headquarters on Tuesday as demonstrators made a bonfire from tobacco leaves in protest against plans to discourage smoking and cut European Union subsidies to tobacco farmers.
Riot police cordoned off the Commission building as thousands of tobacco workers, who fear for their jobs if the subsidy cuts go ahead, staged a noisy protest.

Growers from Spain, Italy, France, Greece and Portugal were joined by production workers, many carrying banners denouncing Health Commissioner Padraig Flynn and Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler, whose proposals will be considered by the Commission on Wednesday.
"The European production of tobacco...is the livelihood of 600,000 families," one banner proclaimed in French.
"Flynn: the new commissioner for unemployment," another said in Italian.
"Our life is tobacco. Our death = reform" (of the tobacco sector), a Spanish banner asserted.
The Commission is expected to propose on Wednesday new action the EU could take to discourage smoking while reforming the controversial tobacco subsidy programme.
But it is not expected to endorse any radical measures such as a complete end to tobacco subsidies or restrictive anti-smoking legislation, EU sources said.
